references.text: The slaughter of the sacrificial animal and the collection of its blood is a parallel to the sacrifice ritual described here.
The ram is slaughtered on the north side of the altar, and the priests dash the blood around on the altar.
Describes the same practice of laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal, slaughtering it, and dashing the blood around on the altar.
Parallel text about dashing the blood around on the altar for peace offerings.
Moses performs exactly what was commanded: he slaughters the ram and dashes the blood around on the altar.
Aaron slaughters the burnt offering, and his sons hand him the blood, which he dashes around on the altar.
Describes the slaughter of the bull and the ram as peace offerings, with dashing of blood around on the altar.
The letter to the Hebrews explains that blood was dashed on the tabernacle and all the vessels used in the service, and that under the law almost everything is cleansed with blood.
Shows how Hezekiah's temple cleansing imitates the specific ritual in the Mosaic Law for dashing the blood of rams.
Confirms that the principle of dashing the blood around the altar also applies to other sacrifice categories (guilt offerings) besides the consecration ram.
Connects the handling of the guilt offering's blood directly to the principle of casting or dashing the blood around the altar.
